sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: There's this 80s movie that I have a real soft spot for.
sentences.zh: 有部八十年代的电影，我特别喜欢。

sentences.en: I saw it in the theater, in fact.
sentences.zh: 其实我当年是在电影院看的。

sentences.en: Now I get to show it to my kids.
sentences.zh: 现在我终于可以把它放给我的孩子看了。

sentences.en: It's a good one, which is a good thing, because when your kids like a movie,
sentences.zh: 这是一部好电影，这绝对是件好事，因为当你的孩子们喜欢上一部电影时，

sentences.en: you end up watching it over and over again.
sentences.zh: 你最后就会陪着他们一遍又一遍地看。

sentences.en: It's called The NeverEnding Story.
sentences.zh: 它叫《大荒无稽》。

sentences.en: The NeverEnding Story?
sentences.zh: 《大荒无稽》？

sentences.en: The NeverEnding Story is a tale of a boy adventurer named...
sentences.zh: 《大荒无稽》讲的是一个少年冒险家的故事……

sentences.en: He and his luck dragon named...
sentences.zh: 他和他的幸运龙……

sentences.en: ...are trying to save the world from the onslaught of a terrible force called...
sentences.zh: 正试图从一种可怕力量的猛烈袭击中拯救世界，这种力量被称为……

sentences.en: Look at Treo!
sentences.zh: 看特雷奥！

sentences.en: The Nothing!
sentences.zh: 虚无！

sentences.en: But this story also takes place inside of a book that's being read by a present-day boy.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事也发生在一个现代小男孩正在阅读的一本书里。

sentences.en: A boy named...
sentences.zh: 一个名叫……

sentences.en: Bastion!
sentences.zh: 巴斯蒂安！

sentences.en: Pretty much all the dialogue in the movie is written with exclamation points.
sentences.zh: 电影里几乎所有的台词都带着感叹号。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Bastion the reader realizes that he is actually written into the story,
sentences.zh: 总之，读者巴斯蒂安意识到自己实际上被写进了故事里，

sentences.en: and it's up to him to save the storybook world.
sentences.zh: 拯救故事书世界的重任落在了他的肩上。

sentences.en: Bastion winds up defeating the Nothing.
sentences.zh: 巴斯蒂安最终战胜了虚无。

sentences.en: Bastion, spoiler alert, by giving the empress of the fantasy world a new name.
sentences.zh: 剧透警告，巴斯蒂安通过给奇幻世界的女皇起了一个新名字赢了。

sentences.en: He has to give me it, but he's chosen it.
sentences.zh: 他不得不把它交给我，但他已经选好了。

sentences.en: He just has to call it out.
sentences.zh: 他只需要喊出来就行。

sentences.en: It's really hard to hear, but he names her Moon Child there.
sentences.zh: 声音真的很轻很难听清，但他在那里给女皇取名叫月亮之子。

sentences.en: I didn't know that for like 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我大概二十年都不知道这一点。

sentences.en: The power of one child's imagination saves an entire world.
sentences.zh: 一个孩子想象力的力量拯救了整个世界。

sentences.en: Seriously, it's a great movie.
sentences.zh: 说真的，这是一部很棒的电影。

sentences.en: Anyway, there is a reason why I'm telling you this story.
sentences.zh: 总之，我给你讲这个故事是有原因的。

sentences.en: I want you to hold on to that idea.
sentences.zh: 我希望你记住这个想法。

sentences.en: That a name can defeat a nothing.
sentences.zh: 一个名字可以战胜虚无。

sentences.en: Okay, with that in mind, here's our producer, Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 好了，带着这个想法，有请我们的制作人萨姆·格林斯潘。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: All right, everyone in listener land.
sentences.zh: 好了，听众朋友们。

sentences.en: Names versus nothings.
sentences.zh: 名字对阵虚无。

sentences.en: When I was a kid growing up in South Florida, there was this beautiful green place where I always wanted to go play.
sentences.zh: 当我在南佛罗里达州长大时，有一个美丽开阔的绿色地方，我一直想去那里玩。

sentences.en: It looked perfect for a kid to run around and throw a ball.
sentences.zh: 那里看起来非常适合小孩子四处奔跑和扔球。

sentences.en: It was a flat-mowed lawn that just stretched into infinity.
sentences.zh: 那是一片修剪平整的草坪，一直延伸到远方。

sentences.en: But my parents wouldn't ever take me there.
sentences.zh: 但我父母从来不带我去那里。

sentences.en: But with good reason.
sentences.zh: 不过这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: It was inside of a giant highway interchange.
sentences.zh: 它位于一个巨大的高速公路立交桥里面。

sentences.en: My five-year-old self would never have been able to convince my parents that this would be a good place to play.
sentences.zh: 五岁的我绝对无法说服我的父母这是一个玩耍的好地方。

sentences.en: Because no responsible parent takes their kid to play catch off the side of I-95.
sentences.zh: 因为没有哪个负责任的父母会带孩子去95号州际公路旁玩接球游戏。

sentences.en: But I don't think I would even have known how to ask them to take me there.
sentences.zh: 但我想我甚至不知道该如何开口请求他们带我去那里。

sentences.en: Because this place isn't really anywhere that we think of as being a place.
sentences.zh: 因为这个地方根本不是我们所认为的“地方”。

sentences.en: There's no name for it.
sentences.zh: 它没有名字。

sentences.en: Let's call it a nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们暂且管它叫“虚无”吧。

sentences.en: As a kid, I couldn't look away from these perfect grassy areas.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我的目光无法从这些完美的草地上移开。

sentences.en: But as I grew up and became a driver, I learned to ignore them like everyone else.
sentences.zh: 但随着我长大了，成为了一名司机，我像其他人一样学会了忽视它们。

sentences.en: So what happens when you give that nothing a name?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你给那个“虚无”赋予一个名字时会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: That's totally what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我完全就是在做这件事。

sentences.en: Giving things a name.
sentences.zh: 给事物赋予名字。

sentences.en: So this is my friend Graham.
sentences.zh: 这位是我的朋友格雷厄姆。

sentences.en: My name is Graham Correll Allen.
sentences.zh: 我叫格雷厄姆·科雷尔·艾伦。

sentences.en: Graham's an artist in Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆是巴尔的摩的一位艺术家。

sentences.en: And he has this project where he's trying to categorize and classify all the different kinds of invisible public spaces that we overlook.
sentences.zh: 他有一个项目，试图对我们忽略的各种隐形公共空间进行归类和分类。

sentences.en: He published a field guide for how to spot them.
sentences.zh: 他出版了一本如何发现它们的实地指南。

sentences.en: It's part of a bigger project called New Public Sites.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名为“新公共场所”的大型项目的一部分。

sentences.en: New Public Sites is an investigation into some of the invisible sites.
sentences.zh: “新公共场所”是对一些隐蔽场所的调查，

sentences.en: and overlooked features of our everyday public spaces within cities that are not traditionally framed as public space.
sentences.zh: 以及城市中我们日常公共空间里那些传统上不被视为公共空间的被忽视的特征。

sentences.en: It's important to name these places because by giving these places succinct and fun and poetic names,
sentences.zh: 给这些地方命名很重要，因为通过赋予这些地方简洁、有趣且富有诗意的名字，

sentences.en: we can help start a discourse about our public spaces and how we want to envision them for the future.
sentences.zh: 我们可以帮助开启关于公共空间的讨论，以及我们希望如何在未来设想它们。

sentences.en: I'm reminded of the never-ending stories.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了《大荒无稽》里的故事。

sentences.en: Bastian, you must give me a name.
sentences.zh: 巴斯蒂安，你必须给我起个名字。

sentences.en: See?
sentences.zh: 看到了吗？

sentences.en: Graham gives these tours where he puts this language to use, describing incredibly boring pieces of the Baltimore landscape.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆进行了这样的参观导览，他运用这些语言，来描述巴尔的摩景观中极其枯燥的部分。

sentences.en: This is the first site along the tour, and here we have a void.
sentences.zh: 这是导览路线上的第一个地点，这里我们有一个“虚空”。

sentences.en: I remember the building that used to stand here.
sentences.zh: 我还记得以前立在这里的那栋建筑。

sentences.en: It was painted blue.
sentences.zh: 它被刷成了蓝色。

sentences.en: Passing through it, you can imagine how us as ghosts, should the building be standing here,
sentences.zh: 穿过它的时候，你可以想象我们作为幽灵，如果这栋建筑还立在这里的话，

sentences.en: would have to actually be invisible to pass through these walls.
sentences.zh: 其实必须隐形才能穿过这些墙壁。

sentences.en: And now it's the reverse.
sentences.zh: 而现在情况正好相反。

sentences.en: The building is the ghost, and we're passing through its walls.
sentences.zh: 建筑变成了幽灵，而我们在穿过它的墙壁。

sentences.en: So Graham is really giving a tour of a vacant lot.
sentences.zh: 所以格雷厄姆实际上是在带大家参观一块空地。

sentences.en: Vacant lot is one way to put it, but notice what Graham called it.
sentences.zh: “空地”是一种说法，但请注意格雷厄姆是怎么称呼它的。

sentences.en: A void.
sentences.zh: 一个“虚空”。

sentences.en: And if you pull up his book that Graham published, sort of a field guide to these new public sites,
sentences.zh: 如果你翻开格雷厄姆出版的那本书，也就是这些新公共场所的实地指南，

sentences.en: you'll see...
sentences.zh: 你会看到……

sentences.en: All right, hang on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，等一下。

sentences.en: Okay, I don't have the book handy, but here it is as a PDF.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我手头没有书，但这里有它的PDF版本。

sentences.en: I'm going to do Command-F, V-O-I-D.
sentences.zh: 我要按Command-F，输入V-O-I-D。

sentences.en: Okay, page 14.
sentences.zh: 好的，第14页。

sentences.en: Void.
sentences.zh: 虚空。

sentences.en: A framed open space imbued with the psychic presence of a former mass...
sentences.zh: 一个被前建筑体量残留的精神存在所浸润的带框开放空间……

sentences.en: ...and or the profound immersion of seductively infinite nothingness.
sentences.zh: 或者说是对具有诱惑力的无限虚无的深沉沉浸。

sentences.en: That certainly is a something.
sentences.zh: 那绝对算是个“东西”。

sentences.en: To find out more about these invisible public spaces,
sentences.zh: 为了解更多关于这些隐形公共空间的信息，

sentences.en: Graham and Sam rode bikes to the edge of East Baltimore to look at a few,
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆和萨姆骑着自行车来到东巴尔的摩的边缘，查看了几个地方，

sentences.en: like the one Sam pined for as a kid.
sentences.zh: 就像萨姆小时候渴望的那样。

sentences.en: It looks like there's a small parting that we can actually see through.
sentences.zh: 看起来有一个我们可以真正看穿的小裂口。

sentences.en: Right now we're at the foot of a small embankment that's probably 15 feet tall or so.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正处于一个小路堤的脚下，大约有15英尺高左右。

sentences.en: We're going to walk up to the edge of this embankment and meet a low-lying concrete wall
sentences.zh: 我们要走到这个路堤的边缘，遇到一堵低矮的混凝土墙，

sentences.en: that will safely separate us from the cloverleaf of traffic.
sentences.zh: 它将把我们与车流交织的苜蓿叶立交桥安全地隔开。

sentences.en: Right beyond this on-ramp onto,
sentences.zh: 就在这个匝道正前方，

sentences.en: we'll be able to hopefully actually look into a freeway eddy.
sentences.zh: 希望我们能真正窥探到一个高速公路回旋涡流。

sentences.en: So let's do that right now.
sentences.zh: 那我们现在就这么做吧。

sentences.en: We're darting across the street during a huge lull in traffic.
sentences.zh: 我们趁着车流稀少的巨大间隙冲过了马路。

sentences.en: So we're looking at, there's this curved highway exit ramp coming in front of us,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，在我们前方有一条弯曲的高速公路出口匝道，

sentences.en: and it's maybe about 15 feet, 20 feet ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 它大概在我们前方15英尺、20英尺的地方。

sentences.en: There's kind of this, almost like a wilderness area.
sentences.zh: 这里有种类似荒野区域的地方。

sentences.en: Fenced in, there's no trespassing by Maryland Transportation Authority.
sentences.zh: 有栅栏围着，马里兰州交通管理局规定禁止入内。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: With the invisible public space in sight, Graham turns to his field manual.
sentences.zh: 随着隐形公共空间进入视野，格雷厄姆翻开了他的实地手册。

sentences.en: Freeway Eddy, an interstitial fragment of space between intersecting curbs of highway pavement.
sentences.zh: 高速公路回旋涡流，是高速公路路面相交路缘之间的一处间隙空间碎片。

sentences.en: And there you have it, that grassy non-place I'd always wanted to hang out in as a kid,
sentences.zh: 你看，我小时候一直想闲晃的那片草地非场所，

sentences.en: now has a name, a freeway eddy.
sentences.zh: 现在有了一个名字，叫做高速公路回旋涡流。

sentences.en: Graham's field guide to new public sites is full of new identities for these kind of places.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆关于新公共场所的实地指南中充满了这类地方的新身份。

sentences.en: So here we have median refuge, a liminal zone of linear respite between parallels of churning traffic.
sentences.zh: 所以这里我们有中央隔离带避难所，这是滚滚车流平行线之间线性喘息的阈限地带。

sentences.en: Enlightened elevation, supple terrain providing the ideal incline
sentences.zh: 启迪高地，提供理想坡度的柔性地形，

sentences.en: from which one may gaze from a wise viewing distance.
sentences.zh: 人们可以从一个明智的观赏距离眺望风景。

sentences.en: Monumental isolation.
sentences.zh: 纪念碑式的孤立。

sentences.en: Big, loose parts.
sentences.zh: 大型松散部件。

sentences.en: Movable materials that invite playful reconfiguration.
sentences.zh: 邀请人们进行趣味性重组的可移动材料。

sentences.en: It is actually an architectural term.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个建筑术语。

sentences.en: Big, loose parts.
sentences.zh: 大型松散部件。

sentences.en: It's a pretty fun-sounding term if you ask me.
sentences.zh: 依我看，这是一个听起来相当有趣的术语。

sentences.en: Parallax of transit.
sentences.zh: 交通视差。

sentences.en: Triangle crossing.
sentences.zh: 三角交叉口。

sentences.en: A three-sided concrete platform or asphalt zone providing solace for street-crossing pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 为过马路的行人提供慰藉的三面混凝土平台或沥青区域。

sentences.en: I don't see too many pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 我没看到太多行人。

sentences.en: We have aural saturation.
sentences.zh: 我们有听觉饱和。

sentences.en: The overwhelming occupation of a surrounding soundscape by sight-generated droning noise.
sentences.zh: 由视觉产生的轰鸣噪音对周围声景的压倒性占据。

sentences.en: Median refuge.
sentences.zh: 中央隔离带避难所。

sentences.en: A liminal pause of restraint.
sentences.zh: 带有克制意味的阈限停顿。

sentences.en: Empty signifier.
sentences.zh: 空洞能指。

sentences.en: A post or pole absent of its original sign and or meaning.
sentences.zh: 失去原有标志和或意义的立柱或杆子。

sentences.en: Sears node.
sentences.zh: 西尔斯节点。

sentences.en: Soil horizon.
sentences.zh: 土壤地平线。

sentences.en: If there's a common theme connecting these sites,
sentences.zh: 如果说这些地点有什么共同的主题，

sentences.en: it's that they're mostly the empty, leftover spaces from car-centered city planning.
sentences.zh: 那就是它们大多是以汽车为中心的城市规划中空置的、剩余的空间。

sentences.en: And it's an odd celebration of these nothing places.
sentences.zh: 这是对这些虚无之地的怪异赞美。

sentences.en: Listen to how Graham describes them.
sentences.zh: 听听格雷厄姆是如何描述它们的。

sentences.en: Beauty, beauty, beauty that one can enjoy.
sentences.zh: 美，人们可以享受的美。

sentences.en: Spectacular and sublime.
sentences.zh: 壮观而崇高。

sentences.en: Quite beautiful.
sentences.zh: 相当美丽。

sentences.en: This is a really beautiful spot.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常美丽的地方。

sentences.en: We're actually standing right now in a long strip of sunlight that is past,
sentences.zh: 我们现在实际上正站立在一长条阳光中，

sentences.en: it's created by the space between these two elevated highways.
sentences.zh: 这是由这两条高架高速公路之间的空间形成的。

sentences.en: We're at the Chinatown bus stop across the street from the Baltimore Travel Plaza.
sentences.zh: 我们在巴尔的摩旅游广场街对面的唐人街巴士站。

sentences.en: Miles outside of the city.
sentences.zh: 距离城市数英里之遥。

sentences.en: Perhaps the most unglamorous way to enter Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 这也许是进入巴尔的摩最不够光鲜亮丽的方式。

sentences.en: And yet it's a gateway for hundreds a week.
sentences.zh: 然而，它却是每周数千人的门户。

sentences.en: And it's a quite beautiful space.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个相当美丽的太空。

sentences.en: Here's where I've got to draw the line, Graham.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆，这就是我要划清界限的地方。

sentences.en: Because there's some trees, there's some birds.
sentences.zh: 因为这里有一些树，有一些鸟。

sentences.en: You know, there's, I guess, some intent of landscaping this area around here.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想这里周围的景观设计是有某种意图的。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it's basically a big parking lot with some trucks with diesel gas across the street.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，它基本上就是一个巨大的停车场，街对面停着几辆烧柴油的卡车。

sentences.en: There's a subway, there's a bus stop.
sentences.zh: 这里有地铁，有公交车站。

sentences.en: What are your grounds for calling this beautiful?
sentences.zh: 你有什么理由称这里为美？

sentences.en: Let's be clear here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里把话说清楚。

sentences.en: You can call that grassy patch off the highway a freeway eddy all you want.
sentences.zh: 你随便把高速公路旁的那片草地叫作高速公路回水湾都行。

sentences.en: But I'm not going to take my kids to play ball in one.
sentences.zh: 但我可不会带我的孩子去那种地方打球。

sentences.en: A highway exit ramp by any other name is still just as unattractive and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 高速公路的匝道换个名字，也一样毫无吸引力且充满危险。

sentences.en: This is beautiful because it's a space that's shared by so many and yet it was completely undesigned.
sentences.zh: 这里很美，因为它是一个被许多人共享的空间，而且完全是自然形成的。

sentences.en: This space was designed as a parking lot.
sentences.zh: 这个空间原本设计为一个停车场。

sentences.en: And it's become this huge nexus for people coming in and out of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 而它已经变成了人们进出巴尔的摩的一个巨大枢纽。

sentences.en: And so it's not necessarily what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以它不一定在于它看起来是什么样。

sentences.en: It's more about what it represents.
sentences.zh: 而更在于它代表了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's no denying that the experience of being in these new public sites is actually pretty terrible.
sentences.zh: 没错，不可否认的是，置身于这些新的公共场所中的体验其实相当糟糕。

sentences.en: But for Graham, the beauty is in their potential.
sentences.zh: 但对格雷姆来说，美感在于它们的潜力。

sentences.en: Sometimes everyday unremarkable spaces can become something more simply by virtue of people being there.
sentences.zh: 有时，日常不起眼的空间只需人们的到来，就能变成更具意义的东西。

sentences.en: It's worth noting here that Zuccotti Park in New York City, the birthplace of the Occupy movement,
sentences.zh: 这里值得一提的是，纽约市的祖科蒂公园，也就是“占领运动”的发源地，

sentences.en: was a privately owned space and not a public park.
sentences.zh: 是一个私人拥有的空间，而不是公共公园。

sentences.en: So if your goal is finding new spaces for engaged democracy to happen, as it is for Graham,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的目标是寻找能让积极参与的民主活动发生的全新空间，就像格雷姆的目标一样，

sentences.en: then you need a way to redefine the places in your neighborhood where that kind of activity can happen.
sentences.zh: 那么你需要一种方式来重新定义你社区中能够发生这种活动的场所。

sentences.en: And I think it's important not to fetishize public spaces as only existing in town squares or Yosemite or Yellowstone or something like this.
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的是，不要将公共空间神圣化，认为它们只存在于城市广场、约塞米蒂或黄石公园之类的地方。

sentences.en: Not just the National Mall in D.C., for example, but any place.
sentences.zh: 例如，不仅是华盛顿特区的国家广场，任何地方都可以。

sentences.en: Our everyday public spaces, you know, the spaces that we all share, it's everywhere and we all have access to it.
sentences.zh: 我们日常的公共空间，你知道的，也就是我们共享的空间，它们无处不在，我们所有人都可以接触到。

sentences.en: These spaces are the places where this happens.
sentences.zh: 这些空间正是这种情况发生的地方。

sentences.en: It doesn't just happen over the Internet.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是通过互联网发生的。

sentences.en: It happens in physical spaces.
sentences.zh: 它发生在实体空间中。

sentences.en: New public sites are these physical spaces that we can appropriate, that we can make our own.
sentences.zh: 新的公共场所就是我们可以占有、可以使其属于我们自己的实体空间。

sentences.en: If it's only for a temporary, you know, demonstration, then so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果这仅仅是为了一个临时的抗议活动，你知道的，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: But maybe it's for a farmer's market.
sentences.zh: 但也许它是为了一个农夫市集。

sentences.en: Maybe it's for a community garden.
sentences.zh: 也许它是为了一个社区花园。

sentences.en: Maybe it's simply for a playground or a place where we need to add a few benches to make it a better bus stop.
sentences.zh: 也许它仅仅是为了一个游乐场，或者是一个我们需要增加几张长椅来使之成为更好公交车站的地方。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, there's potential there.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，那里蕴含着潜力。

sentences.en: And by giving it a name and by starting that conversation, we can kind of get these ideas moving into reality.
sentences.zh: 通过给它起个名字，并通过开启那场对话，我们可以把这些想法转化为现实。

sentences.en: So it all comes back to a name against a nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都归结为用一个名字对抗虚无。

sentences.en: When you give a nothing a name, you can reimagine it as a something.
sentences.zh: 当你给虚无赋予一个名字时，你就可以把它重新想象成某种存在。

sentences.en: If we can create terms for these otherwise invisible experiences and places and things that we all share,
sentences.zh: 如果我们能为这些原本隐形的、我们共同拥有的体验、场所和事物创造术语，

sentences.en: that we all of us share in these public spaces, these new public sites, then it's a starting point.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们所有人都在这些公共空间、这些新的公共场所中共享的东西，那么这就是一个起点。

sentences.en: It's a starting point for that conversation.
sentences.zh: 它是展开那场对话的起点。

sentences.en: By giving it a term, we can then talk about it, and we all know what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 通过给它一个术语，我们就可以谈论它，而且我们都知道我们在谈论什么。

sentences.en: Then that's the first step.
sentences.zh: 那么这就是第一步。

sentences.en: The second step is envisioning, okay, well, how does this need to be improved?
sentences.zh: 第二步是设想，好吧，这需要如何改进？

sentences.en: And the third step is, how do we do that?
sentences.zh: 第三步是，我们该如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: The naming is where it starts.
sentences.zh: 命名就是一切的开端。

sentences.en: I don't know if I named anything Moonchild, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我不知道我是不是把什么东西命名为了“月之子”。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan with help from me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由萨姆·格伦斯潘制作，并在我——罗曼·马尔斯的协助下完成。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 它是旧金山KALW 91.7地方公共广播电台的一个项目。

sentences.en: And the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 以及旧金山美国建筑师学会的项目。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: To find out more about Graham's project and his mobile app, which will help you identify
sentences.zh: 要了解更多关于格雷姆的项目以及他的移动应用，该应用将帮助你识别

sentences.en: and even make up new names for your new public sites in your own backyard,
sentences.zh: 甚至为你自己后院的新公共场所捏造新名字，

sentences.en: check out our website.
sentences.zh: 请查看我们的网站。

sentences.en: It's 99%Invisible.org.
sentences.zh: 网址是99percentInvisible.org。
